intl_finance.document: Bank statement or bank letter (dated within the last six months) showing the account holder's name, account type, currency and balance; a sponsor also submits a Declaration and Certification of Finances (DCF) form with original hand signatures. Total funds must equal or exceed the Estimate of Expenses for the first year.

deadlines.note: August 1 (year not stated on the page)

deadlines.label: ISSO deadline for I-20 request, spring semester admits
deadlines.note: December 15 (year not stated on the page)

intl_finance.notes: The I-20 page lists confirming admission by paying the enrollment deposit as the step before submitting financial documents, and the Visa Document Request E-Form in the UMass VIP portal. The financial documents page itself states no submission deadline. Not accepted: investment accounts, salary confirmation, pay statements, retirement plans, home equity, tax returns. Educational loans need a sanction letter from the provider.

notes: Supplements 'none': the first-year checklist (source 1, for Spring or Fall 2027) lists only a personal essay of 250-650 words, with no college-specific written questions. Applicants may use a Common Application essay option or, on the UMass Lowell application, one of these three prompts: 'What do you do in your spare time?' / 'What is the greatest challenge your generation will face? What ideas do you have for dealing with this issue?' / 'Formulate the perfect admissions essay question and answer it.' These are alternatives to the personal statement, not additional essays, so they are not listed as prompts. Source 3 gives the I-20 sequence (deposit first, then documents); its August 1 and December 15 dates are ISSO visa-document deadlines, not tied to financial documents specifically.
